text: Just at that moment a beautifully dressed boy and girl sat down where the old couple had been, and they were the hero and heroine, of course. <break time="0.8s" /> Still smiling, Miss Brill prepared to listen, but the girl said, No, not now, and the boy asked, But why, Because of that stupid old thing at the end there. <break time="0.8s" /> Why does she come here at all, and who wants her, he went on, Why does she not keep her silly old face at home. <break time="0.8s" /> It is her fu fur which is so funny, the girl giggled, It is exactly like a fried whiting. <break time="0.8s" /> On her way home Miss Brill usually bought a slice of honey cake at the bakers, and it was her Sunday treat, sometimes with an almond in it and sometimes not. <break time="0.8s" /> When there was an almond, it was like carrying home a tiny present, and she would hurry home and strike the match for the kettle in quite a dashing way. <break time="0.8s" /> But today she passed the bakers by, climbed the stairs, went into her little dark room, which was like a cupboard, and sat down on the red eiderdown. <break time="0.8s" /> She sat there a long time, then quickly, without looking, laid the fur inside its box, and when she put the lid on, she thought she heard something crying.
